newsitem.title: ISRAEL: First Int'l Bank eyes acquisition.
newsitem.headline: First Int'l Bank eyes acquisition.

text.p: First International Bank of Israel's plans to acquire another Israeli bank have received approval in principle from the banking commissioner, managing-director Shlomo Piotrkowsky said on Tuesday.

"It will be difficult to grow by way of acquiring a bank -- we don't see too many banks being put up for sale -- but those banks that are put up for sale within the banking groups and fit into our structure and management style, we will consider buying," Piotrkowsky said news conference releasing the bank's 1996 results.
He said he had recently won consent from banking commissioner Ze'ev Abeles to acquire one of several banks likely to be sold in the near future.

He refused to name any acquisition targets. Analysts have said likely targets are Mercantile Discount Bank, which is controlled by Israel Discount Bank, Bank Otsar Hahayal, which is controlled by Bank Hapoalim, and Maritime Bank, the smallest independent commercial bank in Israel.

First International, Israel's fourth largest banking group, sought to acquire Union Bank three years ago when it was privatised and made an offer for Israel General Bank last year. In both cases it was outbid.

Piotrkowsky said he saw an acquisition as a means of hastening growth and improving First International's efficiency. The bank is also looking to develop new business through a credit card joint venture later this year, he said.
